notes.text: This double manuscript leaf, authorial pages 3 and 4), develops conditions on a locally finite indexed pseudo-partition and its map phi to a preordered set: continuity, final/quotient topology, openness, and non-emptiness. It then describes strict stratifications by increasing closed families, intersections, and the condition that X_j be rare in X_i when j<i. These are contents of the source, transcribed without a theorem proof.

The left condition 3 literally reads bar X_j* = union over j≤i of X_j*, followed by pour tt j in I. The same handwritten j is clear in the left subscript and final quantifier, while the bound ends in i. This free/bound-index mismatch is preserved. The source forms were compared with the nearby definition X_i=union over j≤i X_j*; the comparison identifies a local notation discrepancy and does not license emendation.

The left separation criterion ends with the literal les X_i sont loc. fermés, without stars. Earlier the same page assumes the X_i closed, whereas the later right paragraph explicitly refers to X_i* being locally closed. This internal source comparison flags the missing-star possibility for mathematical review, but the unstarred written X_i remains in the transcription. No proof of the asserted equivalence was attempted.

The quoted déf annotation gives X_i minus the union over j<i of X_j, with no preceding X_i*=. The later Moyennant sentence explicitly gives X_i*=X_i minus the union over j<i of X_j*, with a written star on the summand. Both forms are retained. Their equivalence or nonequivalence under the page’s hypotheses has not been established in this reading.

The lower-left discussion is framed by il faut voir comment and concerns a least moderate strict refinement of a partition by locally closed moderate pieces. The author’s question and the revisions after plus petite are preserved, including unresolved state and plurality of the raised strictes. This is not presented as a verified existence theorem.

The landscape source has a central pen divider, two slanted separator strokes on the left and a horizontal left separator. Its isolated upper-right signs are reproduced without assigning them a mathematical role. The authorial numbers are 3 and 4); a thinner lower-left 3 has indeterminate attribution. No written date is visible on this assigned sheet. Pale reversed/show-through matter is not transcribed as foreground text.

The two right-clause parenthesis placements are literal: the quotient criterion has an extra close immediately after X_L* ouvert; the uniqueness parenthesis closes after the first barred X_j*, before the next parenthesized equivalence. Curved insertion leaders at loc. finie, croissante, stratifiantes, and avec l’ordre donné de I are not converted into independent underlining or parentheses. The inserted fermées has a separate lower emphasis stroke with a short left attachment loop.

Openness criterion: For a continuous map f, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B) = closure(f^{-1}(B)) for all B. Continuity supplies the inclusion from the right to the left. Openness supplies the reverse: any neighborhood U of x maps to a neighborhood f(U) of f(x), so f(x) in closure B forces U to meet f^{-1}(B). Conversely this reverse inclusion implies every f(U) is open: if a point y in f(U) were in closure(Y\f(U)), an x in U over y would be in closure(f^{-1}(Y\f(U))), contradicting the open neighborhood U. These checks do not change the source j/i mismatch in its numbered formula.

Local closedness diagnostic: The source identifies each cumulative X_i with a closed union of strata. Such an X_i is automatically locally closed, so the written parenthetical criterion using X_i without a star cannot by itself characterize antisymmetry of the quotient preorder. The intended criterion plausibly concerns X_i^*, but the unstarred ink is retained. This is a diagnostic of the written definitions, not an emendation.

The 3 bis note: Under the page's conditions1,2,4 and local finiteness, the equivalence between nonempty X_i and nonempty X_i^* can be checked locally. The lower closed subsets X_j (j<i) are nowhere dense in X_i under condition4; only finitely many are present near any chosen point by local finiteness. A finite union of closed nowhere dense subsets cannot cover a nonempty open piece of X_i. Thus a nonempty X_i has a point outside their union. This validates the conditional argument of the note without changing its labels or uncertain glyphs.
